items.headline: AI rout spreads to Asia: Nasdaq -5.5% Thursday (steepest since April 2025) on data-center scrutiny fears; Asia tech crumbles Friday
Dollar firms in Asia (DXY ~101.7) as haven flows lift yen to one-week high 157.27; 10Y 4.84%, 2Y 4.47%
Oil up a second day in Asia: Brent ~$99.9 (+1.6%), WTI ~$91.6 (+1.2%) on Hormuz supply worries; still set for ~12% weekly drop
Gold eases to ~$4,063 (-0.6%) as oil rebound fans inflation worries; Dec Fed hike 68% (CME FedWatch)
Eurasia cuts Iran-deal odds to 10% (from 20%), US-attack odds to 60% (from 65%) as Tehran's proposal via Qatar is reviewed
Today: US payrolls + Canada jobs 7:30am CT (NFP fcst 65K, unemp 4.2%; CAD +14.6K), UoM 9:00am, Ueda 10:00am, Bowman 12:15pm, NZ elections 3:45pm, CFTC 2:30pm

NY close: dollar flat (DXY ~101.4, little changed) but Aussie weakest and yen strongest — AUD/USD 0.6935 (-1.02%), USD/JPY 157.82 (-0.38%) — as a tech/chip-led US equity selloff drives haven flows; EUR/USD $1.1225, GBP/USD $1.3467, USD/CHF 0.8158, USD/CAD 1.3989, NZD/USD 0.5597

Oil rebounds after Wednesday's ~9% crash: Brent $97.94 (+3.5%) and WTI $90.64 (+2.8%) as traders reassess the Iran war — Eurasia Group cuts deal odds to 10% (from 20%), renewed US strikes 60%; two tankers and a tug caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz; JPMorgan: global market back in surplus (1.4M bpd Oct)

BoE hikes to 4.00% (8-1, Mann for +50bp), first since Aug 2023; Bailey: not necessarily the first of a series, but the case for another 25bp is 'fairly strong' if the US–Iran conflict stays unresolved; CPI seen near 5% by mid-2027; sterling fades from $1.3506 to $1.3467

Gold $4,124 (+1.6% on the day, two-week high $4,147) holding above $4,100 after Wednesday's +3.4% jump; Dec Fed hike ~80% (CME FedWatch, vs 81.2% this morning) after the 7:30am CT triple beat; payrolls Fri 7:30am CT (consensus ~+60K, unemployment 4.2%) is the next test

Central-bank voices keep December doors open without committing: Lagarde — 'many indicators between now and December' will decide the ECB hike; Macklem (Senate) — further BoC hike possible but 'proceed carefully'; Schlegel — SNB policy rate remains the main tool. Canada Budget 2026 tabled at the close ('Masters of Our Destiny'); headline deficit figure not cleanly verified yet (PBO pre-budget outlook $63.3B)
US data triple beat at 7:30am CT: claims 189K (vs 197K fcst, prev revised to 195K), Q3 productivity +3.6% (vs 2.8%), ULC -0.7% (vs +0.3%); DXY firmer at 101.47 off the ~101.25 Asia low; 10Y 4.904%
BoE hikes to 4.00% (8-1, Mann for +50bp), first rise since Aug 2023; Bailey: not necessarily the last unless the Middle East conflict is resolved; CPI seen near 5% by mid-2027; GBP/USD steady ~$1.347
Dollar slides to a one-month low (DXY ~101.25, lowest since Sep 30) as the midterm sweep cheers global markets; EUR/USD $1.1261, USD/JPY 157.95, 10Y 4.847% (lowest since Sep 10); Dec Fed hike ~80.7%

RBA's Hauser: 'Inflation is too high, whichever measure you use'; public confidence in the RBA's inflation fight eroding; denies his October remarks were aimed at swaying the board; AUD unmoved ~$0.7013
Oil crash extends in Asia: Brent ~$93.65 (-1.03%), WTI ~$86.98 (-1.29%) as traders keep pricing an end to the Iran conflict after the midterm sweep

Dollar edges lower in Tokyo after the midterm sweep — DXY 101.41 (-0.06% overnight), EUR/USD $1.1241, USD/JPY 158.25, GBP/USD $1.3462 after a 7-week high of $1.3503, AUD/USD $0.7010, NZD/USD $0.5627; BoJ September minutes reinforce December hike bets; BoE decides today
USD/CHF ~0.8140 in Asia, a second straight day lower as the dollar slides after the Democratic sweep; Swiss CPI (1.5% y/y) keeps SNB tightening doubts alive; Dec Fed hike ~82% (CME FedWatch)
Oil settlements confirm the crash: Brent $94.62 (-8.67%) and WTI $88.12 (-8.29%) on Nov 4, Brent lowest since Aug 31, as the Democratic sweep fuels bets on an end to the Iran conflict
Gold spot +3.4% to ~$4,061 on Nov 4 (biggest daily gain since mid-August), silver +5.1% to $52.29; early Asia Nov 5 gold ~$4,139 as the dollar hits a one-month low and yields ease
